title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Price increase to $4.08 (+6.0%)
drivers.evidence: Two prior weeks at $4.08 saw sales at 13 (x1.27) and 3 (x0.29). The latter (no promo) is most relevant. Noise-adjusted effect of past price hikes: x0.45 (shrunken from x0.29). A 6% price rise likely reduces sales by ~70% vs baseline.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 10.2. No events are scheduled, but the price is raised 6.0% to $4.08. Past price hikes to $4.08 (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw sales drop to 13 and 3 units respectively—well below baseline. The 2026-10-05 week (same price, no promo) sold 3 units (x0.29 vs baseline), suggesting a strong negative price effect. This week's heatwave (38°C) may boost demand, but candy corn is not a heat-driven product, and no evidence supports a weather lift. The classical uplift model suggests no change, but the price increase is a known demand reducer. No promotion or event justifies a lift. The evidence for price sensitivity is strong and consistent. Adjust downward.

  median 10.2 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 25.3 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 19.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
